But once you fill out all your info, THEN it decides to tell you that you have to pay to use it. $20 a month, or $60 a year. horrible sellout of an app, there are plenty better and free ones to find easily on the app store.

reviews.title: Illinois CDL prep
reviews.text: The theory portion of the lessons was incomplete. It was not nearly sufficient to learn the material or even get any useful supplemental study.  The practice test literally had incorrect and false information as the correct answers for many questions. I was getting 100% on all the tests but still failed my first attempt at the actual IL CLP exam because I was going off of inaccurate information from this app. I studied the IL SOS 184 pg study guide instead and tried to unlearn the false information i learned from this app and I passed with flying colors. If this app was a person, I would yoke them up and make them hurt for wasting my time and making a fool of me.

reviews.title: Needs Better Development
reviews.text: Within the app if you click on the button that says I’m not enjoying this App - you go to an email to support so you can tell them what you think is wrong. In this case, after paying for the subscription I find that Test 1 and Test 2 are identical in the test question pool, only in a different order. Really? What is it with these CDL Apps? Just garbage.

reviews.title: Just use notebooklm
reviews.text: It’s ai. I thought it was really good compared to other apps but then I started to check the questions on google and every other question had an incorrect answer, as well as gave me questions for incorrect states. I did pass my test so It’s good for learning the basics, but I copy and pasted my states driving manual into notebooklm, a free google ai and realized it gave me the exact same question and capabilities this app did for free. The questions were phrased the same too which makes me think that’s what the developers used and just made people pay for it.

reviews.title: Glitchy
reviews.text:
UPDATE: the information was not helpful, as I in fact failed. I got to the test, and was entirely confused as the information was not what I learned. This was advertised as helping study with the drivers manual, however after reading it again IT LEFT OUT AO MUCH INFORMATION. I would get 100% on even the hard practice tests, but it still had none of the information that the actual test had. Just study the manual. I want my money back. 

While the information was helpful, my test and lesson information would disappear, making me do it again to get my certificate of completion. It happened twice. Asking the instructors chat doesn’t work either.

reviews.title: Pay
reviews.text: You have to pay in order to get to lesson 3. Why should people have to pay to learn to drive? Most apps use ads and such to make money. This is just greedy and disgusting especially since most people who use apps like these use it to study for a permit test. Don’t download it if you want to pay $8 a month. (I’m cheap but money is also tight.) Which especially makes it harder for minors who may not have jobs yet but need to learn to drive in order to even get a job—coming from someone who has a rather strict family that requires I get a permit or intermediates so I can drive myself back and forth from place to place and such.

reviews.title: Decent
reviews.text: The material is good to learn but it’s easy to pass the exams and practice tests because the questions are all the same. Every exam I took had the same exact general knowledge questions. Some of the answers I got marked wrong were actually right. They would be marked wrong on practice tests but were right on the exams. Like what to do when coming to a downhill exit ramp … answer was reach a safe speed before going downhill into curve. It marked it wrong and put “don’t downshift until in the curve”. Clearly that’s incorrect. Answers in the same order. And the road signs were always the same ! It’s predictable and doesn’t filter out questions we know with new questions or signs to learn ! Each difficulty level seemed the same. I hope these are the only questions on the test , if so I will ace it in a minute

reviews.title: Not Updated, Lack of Practice Exams
reviews.text: The learning portion went fairly well, going through all the questions but then when it came time for practice exams there's basically only one. It doesn't mix in new questions when you take a new practice exam. My son was able to do the practice exam once and then basically get 100 on it every time because it's the exact same questions. They did not update it based on the 2026 additions to the Tennessee permit test and there's only one previous exam that will load. There should be five according to the app so it really feels like a bait and switch on its usefulness. I spent $30 to have access for six months and at 100% it was not worth it.

reviews.title: Confusing
reviews.text:
I’ve learn and passed everything on this app. Yet I see questions with 3 answers that a driver will acknowledge on the road while driving . But choosing one still gives you the wrong answer.  I’m an experienced driver from another country for 24 years always been precautioned never once was involved in any accidents. 

I just can’t understand the type of questions at the dmv . Some don’t make any sense even tho you put yourself into the question pretending you’re in that situation.  I guess we got to act dumb and enter dumb answers to score ?

reviews.title: Glitchy and far to AI generated.
reviews.text:
Good user interface and if the content was accurate would be a strong app.
Starting with the learning modules- it's essentially one page of general information that doesn't go into the detail of what actually needs to be learnt. 
The test pages are full of glitches where questions don't have answers or the pictures related to the questions are inaccurate.
Considering this is paid for content, ensuring that you have someone reviewing and moderating the content for accuracy is key.
